transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t seem to stay focused anymore. At work I’ll be doing inventory and keep reading the same line, or I’ll go to the supply closet and forget what I went in there for. I’m studying for a supervisor certification too, and it’s been hard to keep anything in my head.
When did you first start noticing these problems with concentration and forgetfulness—has this been a lifelong pattern, or did it start more recently?
It started about three years ago, when the contractor switched us over to rotating evening and overnight shifts at the bigger properties. Before that, I don’t remember having this kind of trouble.
On days when you're working these evening or overnight shifts, how many hours of sleep do you typically get, and do you feel rested afterward?

It varies, but after an overnight shift I’ll lie there tired but kind of wired, so it can take a while to fall asleep. Even when I manage a decent number of hours, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
On your days off, when you're not working evening or overnight shifts, do you still have trouble falling asleep or wake up feeling unrested?
Yeah, even on my days off it doesn’t really feel like it resets. I can be tired and still lie there awake, and when I do sleep for a decent amount of time, I wake up feeling like I hardly slept.

Aside from feeling tired, have you noticed yourself worrying excessively about work, health, or other things—worry that's hard to control—on most days, even when you're not thinking about your sleep schedule?
I’m not really sure I’d call it worrying all the time. Mostly I just know I’m tired and it’s hard to get my sleep back on track.
If you have several days off in a row where you're on a regular daytime schedule with no shift work, does your sleep and morning grogginess improve, or does it stay just as bad?
It stays pretty bad, honestly. Even with a few days off, I can lie there tired but wired, and when I do get enough sleep, I still wake up feeling like I barely rested.

Have you ever had a longer stretch away from work—like a week off or a vacation—where you were on a completely normal daytime schedule the whole time? If so, did your sleep and daytime tiredness fully return to normal during that stretch?

I haven’t really had a long break like that. But even when I’m off for a few days and on a normal schedule, it doesn’t seem to go back to normal. I’m still tired but can’t fall asleep easily, and I wake up feeling like I didn’t get much rest.
Is your sleep trouble worse specifically around the times you switch between day, evening, and overnight shifts, or does it feel equally bad no matter which shift or schedule you're on that week?

It feels bad pretty much regardless, but after an overnight shift it’s especially obvious—I’m exhausted, but I’ll still lie there feeling wired. And even if I get a decent amount of sleep, I wake up like I barely rested.
Over the past month, on how many nights per week—whether you're working days, evenings, or overnights—do you have trouble falling or staying asleep?
Most nights—probably five or six nights a week. I’m tired, but I’ll still have trouble getting to sleep, especially after overnights, and then I wake up feeling like I barely rested.
Has anyone who sleeps near you—like a partner or roommate—ever mentioned that you snore loudly, gasp, or seem to stop breathing for moments while you're asleep?
I’m not really sure. No one’s mentioned anything like that to me, at least not that I can remember.
Do you ever find yourself unintentionally dozing off or falling asleep during the day—like while driving, sitting in meetings, or watching TV—even when you're trying to stay awake?
I don’t usually just nod off during the day. It’s more that I’m worn out, but when I actually try to sleep, especially after overnights, I feel tired but wired and don’t wake up feeling rested.
On your days off, if you take a nap during the day without needing to be up for work, do you actually feel rested afterward?
Not really. Even if I nap or get what seems like enough sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports chronic difficulty initiating and maintaining sleep, non-restorative sleep, and daytime cognitive impairment (poor concentration, forgetfulness) occurring nearly every night (5-6 nights/week) for about three years. Although the onset coincided with a shift to rotating evening/overnight work, the sleep disturbance persists even on days off and during stretches on a normal daytime schedule, arguing against a primary circadian rhythm (shift work) disorder, which would be expected to improve with schedule normalization. There is no evidence of loud snoring, witnessed apneas, or excessive daytime sleepiness/dozing to suggest sleep apnea, and no pervasive uncontrollable worry to support generalized anxiety disorder. The clinical picture is best characterized by chronic insomnia with impaired sleep quality and daytime functional impairment, consistent with Insomnia, unspecified (G47.00).
